cards.key_message: A 21-mile chokepoint is holding India's energy economy hostage — Day 20, no end in sight

sub_messages.text: 42% of India's crude imports transit Hormuz; India imports 88.6% of all crude it consumes
sub_messages.visual_detail: Map of Indian Ocean showing Hormuz chokepoint (marker 1: 21 miles wide, 20M bbl/d), India's west coast refinery ports (marker 2: Jamnagar, Kochi, Mundra), stranded vessel clusters (marker 3: 850 tankers anchored), and alternative route arcs from Russia/West Africa/Americas with voyage-day labels (5-7 days Gulf vs 30-45 days Americas)

sub_messages.text: Operation Epic Fury (Feb 28) killed Khamenei; Iran closed Hormuz within hours — only 21 tankers have crossed in 20 days
sub_messages.visual_detail: Horizontal timeline Day 1–20: Feb 28 (strikes, closure declared), Mar 1 (70% traffic drop), Mar 4 (China exempted), Mar 10 (mine-laying begins), Mar 11 (US sinks minelayers), Mar 12 (21 ship attacks), Mar 17 (Larijani killed), Mar 18 (South Pars struck — RED flash node), Mar 19 (bunker busters, current day)

sub_messages.text: This is the largest oil supply disruption in recorded history — ~8M bbl/d offline vs 4-6M in all prior crises
sub_messages.visual_detail: Horizontal grouped bars comparing 5 crises: 1973 Arab Embargo (4.4M), 1979 Revolution (5.6M), 1990 Gulf War (4.3M), 2019 Abqaiq (5.7M, 2 weeks), 2026 Hormuz (8M, Day 20+). 2026 bar in deep red, others in amber gradient. Duration labels on each bar

cards.source: PPAC FY25-26; S&P Global; Working Document A1/A2/A4

cards.key_message: March 18 changed everything: this is no longer a shipping crisis — it is an energy infrastructure war

sub_messages.text: Israel struck South Pars (world's largest gas field) and Asaluyeh refineries; Iran immediately retaliated against Qatar's Ras Laffan and Saudi Ras Tanura
sub_messages.visual_detail: Gulf region map with 6 strike/retaliation markers: (1) South Pars/Asaluyeh — struck by Israel, two refineries halted; (2) Ras Laffan Qatar — 'extensive damage' from Iranian missiles; (3) Ras Tanura Saudi — drone strike, shut down; (4) Fujairah UAE — drones, fires, port suspended; (5) Shah Gas Field UAE — drone fire; (6) Riyadh — 4 missiles intercepted. Color-code: Israeli strikes in blue, Iranian retaliation in red. Brent price callout box: +3.8% on March 18 alone

sub_messages.text: Iran named 5 specific Gulf facilities as next targets — SAMREF, Jubail, Al Hosn, Mesaieed, Ras Laffan (already hit). Every Indian crude loading terminal is within Fattah-1 hypersonic range
sub_messages.visual_detail: 5 threat cards arranged in priority order: Card 1 — SAMREF Saudi (400K bpd, Aramco/ExxonMobil JV, status: THREATENED); Card 2 — Jubail Petrochemical (world's largest complex, THREATENED); Card 3 — Al Hosn UAE (sour gas, THREATENED); Card 4 — Ras Laffan Qatar (ALREADY HIT — red banner); Card 5 — Mesaieed Qatar (THREATENED). Footer: 'Iran's Fattah-2 hypersonic: Mach 13, 1,500km range — all facilities in envelope'

sub_messages.text: Quick Resolution probability has collapsed to 5-10%; Conflagration (Brent $130-200) is now 30-35% and rising after South Pars strike
sub_messages.visual_detail: Root node: 'Post-South Pars (Day 20)'. Branch 1: Quick Resolution 5-10% → Brent $75-85, 60-90 days to reopen (mine clearance required). Branch 2: Prolonged Standoff 35-40% (BASE) → Brent $100-130, closed Q2, partial Q3. Branch 3: Conflagration 30-35% RISING → Brent $130-200, closed through 2026, Gulf facilities damaged. Branch 4: Regime Change 10-15% → $80-100 initially, 6-12 months. Branch 5: Managed Exit 10-15% → $85-100, 90-120 days. Branches 2 and 3 highlighted with thick borders

cards.source: Tasnim News Agency March 18; Goldman Sachs scenarios; Working Document A5/D17/D19

cards.key_message: India's crude basket at $146.09 is up 112% in 20 days — the import bill is now a macro emergency

sub_messages.text: Indian basket trades $34-38 above Brent because the basket formula (72% Dubai + 28% Brent) is structurally over-exposed to Gulf sour grades — exactly the grades most disrupted
sub_messages.visual_detail: Dual-axis line chart, Jan 2026 to March 19. Line 1 (orange): Indian Crude Basket — flat at ~$69 through Feb, then steep 112% climb to $146.09. Line 2 (grey): Brent — flat at ~$60, climbs 80% to $108-110. Line 3 (red dashed): WTI — $57 to $98-99. Shaded gap region labeled '$34-38/bbl SOUR PREMIUM — structural while Hormuz closed'. Feb 28 vertical dashed line: 'Operation Epic Fury'. March 18 vertical line: 'South Pars Strike'. USD/INR secondary axis: ₹84 → ₹92.64 (record low)

sub_messages.text: At $146/bbl annualized: India's crude import bill hits ~$266B — up $166B from baseline, equivalent to 40% of total import bill
sub_messages.visual_detail: Waterfall: Start bar 'FY25 actual import bill $137B'. Step +$43B: 'Volume growth (5.0M bpd vs prior year)'. Step +$86B: 'Price shock ($146 vs $69 baseline)'. Step +$17B: 'INR depreciation effect (₹92.64 vs ₹84)'. Step +$20B: 'LPG/LNG premium'. Endpoint: '$266B annualized run rate'. Each step labeled with % contribution. Red endpoint bar with warning icon: 'Incremental $129B vs FY25 actual'

sub_messages.text: Every $10/bbl = Rs 1.2-1.5 lakh crore ($14-16B) added to annual import bill; at $146, CAD could reach 2.2% of GDP vs targeted 0.7%
sub_messages.visual_detail: Four gauges side by side: (1) Current Account Deficit — needle at 2.2% of GDP, green zone 0-1%, amber 1-1.5%, red 1.5%+, pointer in deep red; (2) Fiscal Deficit — needle at 4.8% (implied), target line at 4.3%; (3) CPI Inflation — 4.1%+ at $100/bbl, RBI comfort zone 4% marked; (4) GDP Growth — 6.6% at $100 sustained vs 7%+ target. All four needles in amber-red zone

cards.source: PPAC; Bloomberg; BusinessToday; Working Document B6/B10/F30

cards.key_message: 22 Indian ships stranded, LPG queues at 3 AM, 330M households rationed — the crisis is already onshore

sub_messages.text: 22 Indian-flagged vessels carrying 1.7 MMT of energy cargo are stuck west of Hormuz; only 3 made it through (92,700 MT LPG to Mundra/Kandla)
sub_messages.visual_detail: Sankey flow diagram: Left side input node 'Indian Fleet — 22 vessels, 1.7 MMT'. Flow splits: thick orange stream '19 vessels STRANDED' subdivided into crude tankers (4, 1.67MMT crude), LPG tankers (6, 320K MT), LNG (1, 200K MT), containers/bulk (8, general). Thin green stream '3 vessels TRANSITED' → Shivalik (45K MT LPG), Nanda Devi (46.5K MT LPG), Jag Ladki → Mundra/Kandla. Bottom footnote: '611 seafarers confirmed safe'. China comparison node: '11 vessels transited freely'

sub_messages.text: LPG is India's most acute vulnerability: 90% of imports transit Hormuz, serving 330M+ households; commercial allocation cut 80%, cylinder refill gap 25-45 days
sub_messages.visual_detail: LPG tank visualization: Full tank outline showing 100% demand. Filled section 'Domestic production 40% (boosted +38% via ESMA directive)'. Emergency import section 'Non-Gulf emergency procurement (US/Norway/Canada/Algeria) ~5-8%'. Empty/crisis zone 'Supply gap ~52-55%'. Gauge needle for refill wait: urban 25 days (amber), rural 45 days (red). Callout boxes: 'Black market: Rs 4,000/cylinder vs regulated Rs 913', '50,000 hotels/restaurants in MP alone with no gas', '741 cylinders seized in Chhattisgarh'

sub_messages.text: India's total reserve cover is 74 days — government refused IEA/G7 SPR release, signaling expectation of prolonged disruption beyond summer
sub_messages.visual_detail: Stacked bar chart: India's 74-day cover broken into SPR 9.5 days (dark blue, 5.33 MMT / 36.92M barrels) and commercial stocks 64.5 days (lighter blue). Comparison bars for Japan (90 days IEA standard + now releasing 80M barrels), South Korea (contributing to IEA release), China (no release needed — Hormuz access). Annotation: 'India declined IEA 400M barrel coordinated release — contrast with 2021 when India released 5M barrels'. Red warning at 74-day mark: 'Day 74 = early June — monsoon season, election pressures'

cards.source: MEA; PPAC; Bloomberg; CNN; Working Document B7/B8/B9/C14

cards.key_message: India's 70% non-Hormuz claim is half-true — 1.3M bbl/d of medium-heavy sour crude and 90% of LPG have no substitute

sub_messages.text: India redirected crude flows impressively — but the grade mismatch is structural: non-Hormuz sources are light/sweet while Indian refineries are built for medium-heavy sour Gulf grades
sub_messages.visual_detail: Sankey: Left input nodes by source — Russia 25-36% (blue, non-Hormuz), Iraq 20-24% (red, HORMUZ), Saudi 14-16% (red, HORMUZ), UAE 5-7% (red, HORMUZ), West Africa 8-10% (green, non-Hormuz), Americas 5-8% (green, non-Hormuz). Center split: 'NON-HORMUZ 70%' (green) vs 'HORMUZ-DEPENDENT 30%' (red). Right output to India refineries. Below the Sankey: second flow showing LPG — 90% Gulf-origin in red, 10% other in green. Label: 'Crude looks diversified; LPG/LNG does not'

sub_messages.text: Russia's discount flipped to a premium: Urals went from $13/bbl below Brent in February to $4-5/bbl ABOVE Brent in March — a $17-18/bbl cost swing per barrel
sub_messages.visual_detail: Two side-by-side comparison groups. Group 1 'Urals vs Brent spread': Feb bar at -$13 (below zero line, green, 'discount'), March bar at +$4-5 (above zero line, red, 'premium'). Swing arrow: '$17-18/bbl reversal'. Group 2 'All-in delivered price Vadinar': Feb ~$55/bbl, March $98.93/bbl (Argus March 14). OFAC waiver note: 'Waiver expires April 3 — 15 days'. Footnote: '60-100M barrels floating in Arabian Sea (Nomura) — still accessible if waiver renewed'

sub_messages.text: The Russia waiver (April 3) is the single most urgent forcing function: 25-36% of Indian imports depend on it, and renewal is probable but explicitly conditioned on buying US crude
sub_messages.visual_detail: Countdown timeline from March 19 to May 31. Key nodes: March 19 'TODAY — Day 20, $146 basket'; April 3 'RUSSIA WAIVER EXPIRES — 30M barrels secured, next batch at risk' (red flash); April 26 'Chabahar port waiver decision' (amber); April TBD 'OPEC+ meeting — irrelevant if Hormuz closed'; May 'Q4 FY26 earnings — OMC devastation visible'; May-June 'Kharif planting — fertilizer crunch, 50% world urea disrupted'. All nodes color-coded: Red = urgent, Amber = watch, Grey = lower priority. Bessent quote bubble at April 3: 'We fully anticipate New Delhi will ramp up purchases of US oil'

cards.source: Argus Media; OFAC; Treasury Sec Bessent statements; Nomura; Working Document C11/C12/C13/F26

cards.key_message: Even after ceasefire, the Strait stays closed: mine clearance takes 51+ days with degraded Western minesweeping capacity

sub_messages.text: Iran deployed EM-52 Chinese-supplied rocket-propelled rising mines (300kg warhead, defeats conventional minesweeping) plus SADAF-01 contact mines — insurer risk pricing alone paralyzes traffic
sub_messages.visual_detail: Three mine type cards: Card 1 — EM-52 (Chinese): Rocket-propelled, acoustic sensors, 300kg warhead, NON-MAGNETIC composites defeat conventional sweeping — threat level: CRITICAL (red). Card 2 — SADAF-01: Traditional moored contact mines, cheap/numerous, sweepable but labor-intensive — threat level: HIGH (orange). Card 3 — Bottom-influence: Magnetic/acoustic/pressure triggered, hardest to detect — threat level: HIGH (orange). Footer stat: '2,000-6,000 mines in pre-war arsenal; ~10 confirmed in strait but threat effect = 100% traffic suppression'

sub_messages.text: Historical benchmark: Operation Desert Storm 1991 took 51 days to clear 907 mines off Kuwait — WITH minefield maps from defeated Iraq, AFTER war ended; no maps exist for Hormuz
sub_messages.visual_detail: Phased horizontal timeline post-hypothetical ceasefire: Phase 0 'Ceasefire declared (Day X)'; Phase 1 '0-7 days: Hasty single-lane clearance attempt — high risk, limited insurance'; Phase 2 '7-30 days: Minimum confidence corridor — some VLCC transits, war risk premium >5%'; Phase 3 '30-60 days: Sustained clearing — still not complete, GCC export ramp begins'; Phase 4 '60-120 days+: Full sweep — possibly never complete (WWII mines still surfacing). Desert Storm 1991 benchmark: 51 days for 907 mines WITH maps.' UK minesweeper note: 'Royal Navy pulled last Gulf minesweeper home days before Iran mined the strait'

sub_messages.text: No active negotiations exist — Trump 'not ready to deal,' Iran FM rejects ceasefire entirely; the 51-day clock hasn't even started
sub_messages.visual_detail: Split screen quote cards. Left side (Trump, March 15, red): 'Iran wants to make a deal, and I don't want to make it because the terms aren't good enough yet.' Right side (Iran FM Araghchi, March 15, dark green): 'We never asked for a ceasefire, and we have never asked even for negotiation.' Below the quotes: Iran's 3 ceasefire conditions listed — (1) Recognition of nuclear rights + regional influence, (2) Reparations for 1,200+ killed and thousands of sites struck, (3) Binding international guarantees against future aggression. Footer: 'Assessment: These are non-starters for Washington. Clock at Day 20 — mine clearance Day 0 not yet reached'

cards.source: Columbia University; CNN; CBS News; US Naval Institute; Working Document D16/D18

cards.key_message: ACT 2 — CEO LANE: The refinery complexity hierarchy has never mattered more; your position in it is your destiny for the next 6 months

sub_messages.text: Nelson Complexity Index is now a real-time P&L determinant — NCI 21.1 (Jamnagar) prints money at $146; NCI 5.6 (HPCL Mumbai) is burning cash
sub_messages.visual_detail: X-axis: Nelson Complexity Index (4 to 22). Y-axis: Estimated GRM at $146/bbl crude (negative $2 to positive $15). Bubble size: refinery capacity in MMTPA. Named bubbles: Jamnagar DTA+SEZ (NCI 21.1, GRM ~$12-15, huge bubble, green); Panipat IOCL (NCI 13.7, GRM ~$6, medium, amber); Paradip IOCL (NCI 12.2, GRM ~$5); Nayara Vadinar (NCI 12.8, GRM ~$5); HMEL Bathinda (NCI 12.6); Kochi (NCI 10.8, GRM ~$2, amber-red); MRPL Mangalore (NCI 10.6); Vizag HPCL (NCI 7.8, GRM ~-$1, red); BPCL Mumbai (NCI ~6, GRM ~-$3, red); HPCL Mumbai (NCI 5.6, GRM ~-$4, deep red). Vertical dashed line at NCI 12: 'Crisis Survival Threshold'. Horizontal dashed line at GRM=0: 'Breakeven'

sub_messages.text: The strategic question for the next 6 months: Are you RIL (exporting 60% at market prices, insulated) or PSU OMC (retail price-frozen, bleeding cash above $100/bbl)?
sub_messages.visual_detail: Matrix: X-axis 'Crude Processing Flexibility (Low→High NCI)'; Y-axis 'Revenue Pricing Freedom (Regulated→Market)'. Quadrant labels: Top-right (HIGH/MARKET): 'Crisis Winners — RIL Jamnagar, Nayara (partial)'; Top-left (LOW/MARKET): 'Structural Reform Required'; Bottom-right (HIGH/REGULATED): 'Complexity Invested, Returns Capped — IOCL Panipat/Paradip, BPCL'; Bottom-left (LOW/REGULATED): 'Crisis Casualties — HPCL Mumbai, BPCL Mumbai'. Company logos/names plotted in each quadrant with current GRM estimate

sub_messages.text: ESMA override is non-negotiable: all C3/C4 streams go to OMCs for LPG — no petrochemical diversion permitted, regardless of margin optimization plans
sub_messages.visual_detail: Waterfall showing product slate value destruction at Rs 3,000/MT naphtha vs Rs 1,800/MT LPG equivalent: Start 'Optimized product slate (pre-ESMA) base value 100'. Drop '-18%: LPG yield maximization mandate (ESMA March 5)'. Drop '-8%: Grade substitution losses (no heavy sour available)'. Drop '-6%: Throughput reduction (wrong crude diet)'. Recovery '+4%: Government LPG supply compensation (partial)'. End state: '72% of pre-crisis product slate value'. ESMA directive date: March 5, 2026

cards.key_message: Every $5/bbl increase wipes 55-62% of OMC earnings — but the real divergence is between complexity tiers, not just oil price

sub_messages.text: UBS analysis: IOC loses Rs 153B PAT per $5/bbl (55% of FY27 consensus); BPCL Rs 98B (51%); HPCL Rs 88B (62%) — UBS has downgraded HPCL to SELL with target cut 37% to Rs 340
sub_messages.visual_detail: Three parallel waterfall charts side by side, one per OMC. IOC: Start Rs 278B FY27 consensus PAT → each $5/bbl step (-Rs 153B) shown as red drop steps at $100 ($125B remaining), $110 ($0), $120 (-$28B), $146 (-$118B). BPCL: similar structure starting Rs 192B. HPCL: most aggressive drop — Rs 142B start, at $100 already near zero, at $146 deeply negative. Current crude price marker at $146 shown as vertical red line across all three charts. UBS rating labels below: IOC 'NEUTRAL', BPCL 'NEUTRAL', HPCL 'SELL (Rs 340 target)'

sub_messages.text: RIL Jamnagar (NCI 21.1) has no meaningful breakeven — Singapore GRM jumped from $3.4 to ~$30/bbl; processing 216+ crude grades means maximum flexibility to capture the crisis premium
sub_messages.visual_detail: Dual-line chart from Jan to March 19. Line 1 (green, RIL): Singapore complex GRM proxy — flat at $3.4 pre-crisis, shoots to ~$30/bbl post-Feb 28. Line 2 (red, PSU OMC average): GRM — starts $6-8/bbl, declines to $0-3 range at $146 crude. Shaded region between lines: 'NCI premium — value of complexity'. Inset text: 'Jamnagar processed 216+ crude grades — maximum substitution flexibility'. OMC marketing margin shown separately: -Rs 19.8/litre (Nomura)

sub_messages.text: CEO action: Stress-test refinery throughput for zero-Gulf-crude scenario; model the NCI upgrade ROI at $120-150 Brent — the payback period has never been shorter
sub_messages.visual_detail: Three CEO decision scenario cards: Card 1 'If Brent sustains $120-130 (Prolonged Standoff)': NCI 5-6 refineries at -$3 to -$5 GRM, FCC/hydrocracker upgrade IRR = 45-60% at these prices vs 18% pre-crisis. Card 2 'If Brent hits $150-200 (Conflagration)': Government forced price rise — retail unfreeze likely above Rs 120-130/litre threshold; NCI premium widens to $15+/bbl. Card 3 'If Brent returns to $75-85 (Quick Resolution — 5-10% probability)': Upgrade economics still robust; crisis-demonstrated the risk. CEO checklist below: (1) Model NCI upgrade ROI at $120/$150 Brent by board meeting; (2) Identify fastest-to-commission hydrocracker/FCC additions; (3) Review Vizag RUF ($2.5/bbl GRM addition) as proof of concept

cards.source: UBS March 9; Nomura; Working Document E22/E23/E24

cards.key_message: The 41-day procurement window is closing: lock Russian barrels before April 3, pre-position West Africa and Brazil now, accept the grade mismatch

sub_messages.text: Available alternative supply hierarchy: Angola (254K bpd active), Nigeria (142K bpd), Brazil BPCL deal (12M barrels FY27 at $780M), Guyana (emerging), US (available but politically conditioned on crude purchase commitment to Washington)
sub_messages.visual_detail: X-axis: Supply availability speed (Days to first cargo, 15-45 days). Y-axis: Volume available to India (kbpd). Bubble size: grade compatibility with Indian refinery slate (bigger = more compatible). Named bubbles: Russia Urals (fastest 15-20 days, 1,200 kbpd potential, medium bubble — waiver expiry April 3 red warning); Angola (25 days, 254K bpd, large bubble — good heavy sour match); Nigeria (25 days, 142K bpd, medium); Brazil (35-40 days, 200K bpd growing, medium — BPCL deal noted); Guyana (40-45 days, 80K bpd, small); US WTI (35-40 days, 500K bpd available, small bubble — light sweet mismatch + political condition). Vertical red line at 15 days: 'April 3 Russia waiver deadline'

sub_messages.text: Brazil is the emerging anchor: BPCL's $780M deal for 12M barrels (FY27) is the template — Buzios/Tupi medium-sweet grades run at 70-80% yield in complex refineries vs 95%+ for Gulf sour
sub_messages.visual_detail: Side-by-side comparison bars for 4 crude grades vs Indian refinery design spec. Metric: Distillate yield at NCI 12+ refinery. Iraq Basra Heavy: 94% (pre-crisis supply, now blocked). Saudi Arab Medium: 91% (Hormuz, threatened). Russian Urals: 86% (non-Hormuz, waiver). Brazil Buzios: 78% (non-Hormuz, no sanctions). Guyana Liza: 75% (non-Hormuz). US WTI: 68% (light sweet penalty at complex refinery). Bars annotated with voyage days to India west coast. Design spec reference line at 90%: 'Grade match threshold for full-yield operation'

sub_messages.text: CEO checklist — next 10 days: (1) Lock Russian spot cargoes before April 3; (2) Activate Petrobras framework for accelerated Brazil delivery; (3) Tender 4-6 West Africa/Brazil cargoes this week; (4) Model INR 88-95 FX hedge for entire import program
sub_messages.visual_detail: 10-day action timeline March 19-29 with CEO-specific milestones: Day 1 (March 19-TODAY): 'Authorize emergency West Africa/Brazil spot tender — 4-6 cargoes'. Day 3 (March 22): 'Close Russian spot procurement — every barrel at Urals +$5 vs $146 basket'. Day 5 (March 24): 'Activate BPCL-Petrobras accelerated delivery protocol for 12M barrel FY27 contract'. cards.key_message: Prepare for the Gulf facility scenario: if Ras Tanura, Jubail, or Mesaieed take direct hits, non-Hormuz diversification is not enough — you need non-Gulf supply entirely

sub_messages.text: Iran's IRGC has named 5 Gulf facilities as next targets; 4 have already been attacked (Ras Laffan, Ras Tanura, Fujairah, Shah Gas) — India's top crude loading terminals are all within Fattah-2 hypersonic range
sub_messages.visual_detail: Gulf region map with concentric range circles from Iran's western missile sites: Inner circle (500km) — Basra, Kuwait, Ras Tanura; Middle circle (1000km) — Jubail, Fujairah, Muscat; Outer circle (1500km) — Ras Laffan Qatar, Mumbai coast. Color coding: RED markers — already struck (Ras Laffan, Ras Tanura, Fujairah, Shah Gas). ORANGE markers — explicitly threatened (SAMREF, Jubail, Al Hosn, Mesaieed). GREEN markers — not yet threatened (Basra VLCC terminal, Kuwait Ahmadi). India flag markers on west coast showing refinery cluster. Arrows showing typical VLCC loading routes to Jamnagar/Kochi

sub_messages.text: Stress-test scenario: If Gulf loading terminals are damaged for 6 months, India must source 100% of imports from Russia (waiver-dependent), West Africa, Americas — accepting 30-45 day voyage economics and grade mismatches costing $8-15/bbl in yield loss
sub_messages.visual_detail: CEO stress-test waterfall: Start 'Current procurement cost at $146/bbl (100% baseline)'. Step 'Switch to 100% non-Gulf supply': +$12-15/bbl grade mismatch yield loss. Step 'Freight premium (30-45 day voyages vs 5-7 day)': +$4-6/bbl. Step 'Vessel availability premium (VLCCs redirected from ME)': +$3-5/bbl. Partial offsets: '-$8/bbl: No Hormuz war risk surcharge'; '-$5/bbl: Russia waiver if renewed at discount'. Net end state: 'All-in cost ~$152-158/bbl even with non-Gulf supply — not a price solution, a supply security solution'. Recommendation box: 'Accept the cost; model refinery throughput reduction to 85-90% until grade supply stabilizes'

sub_messages.text: CEO board brief must cover dual scenario: Prolonged Standoff (35-40%, Brent $100-130) AND Conflagration (30-35%, Brent $130-200) — the gap between them is Gulf facility damage, not just Hormuz duration
sub_messages.visual_detail: Two CEO-facing scenario deep-dive cards side by side. LEFT: 'BASE CASE — Prolonged Standoff (35-40%)': Brent $100-130, Hormuz closed Q2/partial Q3, Gulf terminals operational (mostly), India supply gap manageable with Russia+West Africa+Americas, NCI 12+ refineries profitable, OMCs need partial retail price rise. Checklist: Lock supply, hedge at backwardation, upgrade ROI modeling. RIGHT: 'WATCH CASE — Conflagration (30-35% and RISING after March 18)': Brent $130-200, Gulf terminals damaged, India supply gap becomes structural, government forced retail price liberalization >Rs 120/litre, NCI 5-6 refineries non-operational, SPR drawdown begins Day 50+. Checklist: Non-Gulf supply 100% contingency, emergency capacity-sharing with IOCL, government subsidy modeling

cards.source: IRGC Tasnim March 18; Goldman Sachs; Working Document D17/D20/G34

cards.key_message: ACT 2 — CFO LANE: The balance sheet is being attacked from three directions simultaneously — crude cost, currency, and working capital

sub_messages.text: Indian crude basket $146.09 × INR 92.64 = ₹13,529/barrel import cost vs ₹5,797/barrel in February — a 133% cost increase in 20 days
sub_messages.visual_detail: Three grouped before/after bars, Feb vs March 19. Bar 1 'Crude basket USD': Feb $69.01 → March $146.09 (+112%). Bar 2 'USD/INR rate': Feb ₹84 → March ₹92.64 (+10.3%). Bar 3 'All-in INR import cost per barrel': Feb ₹5,797 → March ₹13,529 (+133%). Each bar with percentage change callout. Footer: 'Combined effect: every rupee of INR depreciation adds ~₹1,800 crore to annual OMC import bill at 5M bpd import volume'

sub_messages.text: Working capital is being destroyed in three loops: crude payment at 30-day credit is now 2.5x larger; vessel hire/war risk insurance has tripled; LPG compensation arrears from government will take 6-12 months to settle
sub_messages.visual_detail: CFO working capital waterfall: Start 'Feb 2026 monthly working capital requirement: Rs X (100 baseline)'. Step +87%: 'Crude cost increase (volume × basket price change)'. Step +23%: 'INR depreciation on USD payables'. Step +18%: 'War risk insurance premium (P&I clubs 3x)'. Step +12%: 'Vessel hire rate premium (VLCC $200K+ vs $35K pre-crisis)'. Step -15%: 'Credit line expansion (assumed)'. Step -8%: 'Payment term extension negotiations (partial)'. End state: 'Working capital requirement 237% of February level'. Warning box: 'Government LPG compensation = Rs 2-3/litre underrecovery at Rs 913 cylinder — cash flow impact 6-12 month lag'

sub_messages.text: Hedging signal: steep backwardation (WTI $99 prompt vs $69 Dec 2026 vs $58 2027) means the market expects the shock to be temporary — CFOs have a 60-day window to lock deferred supply at $69-75 before the curve moves
sub_messages.visual_detail: Oil futures curve chart: X-axis = time (March 2026 to Dec 2027). Y-axis = price/barrel. Steep downward-sloping curve: March $99 → June $89 → Sept $79 → Dec 2026 $69 → Mar 2027 $63 → Dec 2027 $58. Labels: 'BACKWARDATION — market pricing temporary shock'. Comparison flat line: 'IEA base forecast $70 long-run'. Key annotation: 'Lock Dec 2026 forward at $69 = hedge at 53% below today's basket'. cards.key_message: Use the backwardation: lock deferred crude at $69-75 (Dec 2026) — this is the cheapest hedge window before the curve reprices on ceasefire news or waiver renewal failure

sub_messages.text: Market structure in extreme backwardation offers a once-in-a-decade opportunity: Dec 2026 WTI at $69 represents a 53% discount to today's basket — but the trade will unwind violently on ceasefire headlines

cards.key_message: Day 20: The largest oil supply disruption in history just became an energy infrastructure war — and India is in the crossfire

sub_messages.text: Indian crude basket at $146.09/bbl — up 112% since Feb 28. Annualised import bill now exceeds $200 billion.
March 18 changed everything: South Pars struck, Ras Laffan hit, Ras Tanura shut. This is no longer a shipping disruption — it is deliberate destruction of global energy infrastructure.
You have 41 days before the Russia waiver expires, the non-alignment window closes, and OMC balance sheets break. The clock is running.

cards.source: PPAC FY25-26; Argus Media March 19, 2026; OFAC General License

cards.key_message: Hormuz carries 30% of global seaborne oil — and it has effectively stopped moving

sub_messages.text: Only 21 tankers transited the strait since Feb 28. March 14 was the first full day with zero AIS-confirmed crossings. 850 tankers are clustered in the region.
125 million barrels of oil are physically stranded in the Gulf. 150+ vessels anchor outside the strait. Major shipping lines — Maersk, CMA CGM, Hapag-Lloyd — have suspended all transits.
This is the largest supply disruption in history: ~8M bbl/d offline vs 5.7M in 1990 Gulf War. And it has no end date.

cards.source: S&P Global Platts; Kpler; IAEA shipping data; March 19, 2026

cards.key_message: India imports 88.6% of its crude — and 42% of that moves through the strait that just closed

sub_messages.text: India is the world's 3rd-largest oil importer at ~5.0M bbl/d. Domestic production covers only 11.4% of demand. FY25 import bill: $137 billion.
Over 60% of crude imports originate from Persian Gulf states — Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, UAE — all of whose loading terminals are now inside the conflict zone.
Every $10/bbl increase adds $14–16 billion to the annual import bill. At $146 basket, annualised import cost exceeds $200 billion — 40% of India's total import bill.

cards.source: PPAC FY25-26; OPEC 2026; Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas

cards.key_message: Russia's discount flipped to a premium — India's single largest supply lifeline just got $17–18/bbl more expensive

sub_messages.text: Urals went from $13/bbl discount to $4–5/bbl premium vs Brent after the crisis began. Delivered price to India's west coast: $98.93/bbl (Argus, March 14). The arbitrage is dead.
The OFAC general license (March 5) allowed ~30 million barrels purchased in one week — Reliance and IOC each bought ~10M barrels. But the waiver expires April 3. No renewal confirmed.

Treasury Secretary Bessent's signal: renewal is 'not the last of its kind' but contingent on India ramping up US crude purchases. A political price tag is attached to every Russian barrel after April 3.

quotes.quote: We fully anticipate that New Delhi will ramp up purchases of US oil
quotes.context: Condition attached to possible waiver renewal

cards.source: Argus Media March 14; OFAC; The Wire; US Treasury statements

cards.key_message: India's 70% 'non-Hormuz' claim is real for crude — but hides a 1.3M bbl/d gap that no alternative can fill

sub_messages.text: Non-Hormuz crude share rose from ~55% to ~70% post-crisis. But this masks the grade mismatch: Indian refineries are built for medium-heavy sour Gulf grades. West African and US shale crudes are light-sweet — they don't fill the same barrel.

~1.3–1.5M bbl/d of medium-heavy sour crude from Iraq Basra Heavy and Saudi Arab Medium/Heavy is structurally irreplaceable. Switching forces refineries below capacity and destroys heavy product yields.
Americas-sourced crude takes 30–45 days to reach India vs 5–7 days from Gulf. Voyage economics alone add $3–5/bbl at current freight rates — before any grade discount adjustment.

cards.source: PPAC; S&P Global Platts; Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas

cards.key_message: India's total reserve cover is 74 days — and the government's refusal to release SPR signals it expects disruption to last longer

sub_messages.text: SPR holds 5.33 MMT (36.92M barrels) — just 9.5 days of cover. Commercial OMC stocks add ~64.5 days. Total: 74 days. Every day the strait stays closed, the buffer shrinks.

India refused to participate in the IEA's 400M barrel coordinated release — the largest in 50-year history. Government rationale: 'India First.' Real signal: 74 days buys time only if disruption is temporary.
The IEA release itself is only ~20 days of lost Hormuz volume and takes 120 days to fully deliver. It may calm markets but cannot fix the physical disruption.

cards.source: PPAC; IEA Strategic Reserve announcement; Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas

cards.key_message: 330 million households. 3 AM queues. 90% of LPG imports through a closed strait — India's cooking gas crisis is now acute

sub_messages.text: India imports ~60% of its LPG consumption (~18.5 MMT/year), and 90% of those imports transit Hormuz. Qatar alone provides one-third of all LPG imports. There is no alternative at scale.
Commercial LPG allocation cut 80% from March 12. Domestic cylinder refill gap: 25 days urban, 45 days rural. Cylinder price hiked Rs 60. Black market at Rs 4,000 vs regulated Rs 913.
sub_messages.emphasis: 80% commercial cut; Rs 913 → Rs 4,000 black market

sub_messages.text: Ground reality: 3 AM queues at distribution centers, fistfights, 50,000 hotels/restaurants in MP alone starved of gas, households reverting to firewood. This is a humanitarian pressure point, not just a supply metric.

cards.source: PPAC; Bloomberg; CNN; Petroleum Ministry LPG Control Order March 8

cards.key_message: Government invoked ESMA on March 8 — refiners have no choice but to maximize LPG output, regardless of margin impact

sub_messages.text: Under the Essential Services Maintenance Act, all C3/C4 hydrocarbon streams — propane, butane, propylene, butenes — must flow exclusively to OMCs for cooking gas. No petrochemical diversion permitted.
Domestic LPG production surged 38% within days of the directive. Refineries operating under a government-mandated product slate — this is a direct override of optimization decisions.

The consequence: naphtha and petrochemical yields are sacrificed. Refineries optimized for petrochemical integration — IOCL Panipat, BPCL Bina, RIL Jamnagar — face statutory constraints on their highest-margin output streams.

cards.key_message: Only 3 ships have broken through — delivering 92,700 MT LPG against a monthly import need of ~1.5 MMT

sub_messages.text: MV Shivalik, MV Nanda Devi, and Jag Ladki delivered a combined 92,700 MT LPG to Mundra and Kandla under Indian Navy escort. Each transit was individually negotiated with Iran — there is no blanket deal.
6 LPG tankers remain stranded west of the strait, carrying 320,000 MT of LPG. That cargo alone represents roughly 3 weeks of current rationed urban supply.
Emergency LPG procurement from US, Norway, Canada, and Algeria has only reduced Gulf LPG dependence from 90% to ~70%. Non-Gulf alternatives simply do not exist at the required scale or speed.

cards.key_message: China gets blanket passage; India gets case-by-case. Non-alignment delivers half-measures while Beijing extracts full dividends

sub_messages.text: Iran exempted Chinese vessels from the Hormuz closure. China has transited 11 vessels since March 1. India has transited 3, Pakistan 1, Japan zero, South Korea zero. Non-alignment's concrete yield: marginally better than aligned US allies, far worse than China.
India's warships escort vessels AFTER they exit the strait. The Navy is not forcing passage. Every LPG tanker transit depends on Iran's daily goodwill — which can be withdrawn without notice.

India refused the IEA SPR release. India has not condemned the US-Israel strikes. India is threading a needle — but the thread is fraying as US pressure to align intensifies ahead of the April 3 waiver deadline.

sub_messages.emphasis: South Pars: ~33% of India's LPG sourced here

sub_messages.emphasis: Ras Laffan hit — Qatar's LPG export hub damaged

sub_messages.text: India imports approximately 40% of its fertilizer requirements from the Middle East (MUFG). Urea, DAP, and MOP shipments all transit Hormuz or originate from Gulf chemical complexes now under threat.

Kharif planting season begins May–June 2026. Fertilizer must be procured, shipped (30–45 days from alternatives), and distributed to 120+ million farm holdings before soil preparation begins. The procurement window is closing now.

sub_messages.text: South Pars strike has halted Iran's gas flows to Iraq. Iraq depends on Iranian gas for 30–40% of its electricity. Power outages cascade into petrochemical and fertilizer plant shutdowns — and into Iraq's crude production capacity.

sub_messages.text: The second-order loop: Iraq's fertilizer exports (urea from gas feedstock) also originate from the same gas infrastructure. One strike on South Pars has simultaneous crude, power, and fertilizer consequences for India.

sub_messages.text: South Pars produces approximately 70% of Iran's natural gas and is the shared reservoir underlying Qatar's North Field — the source of most of the world's LNG. European gas benchmark surged 30% within 48 hours of the strike.
India's LNG imports are relatively small but concentrated: Qatar ships virtually all its LNG through Hormuz. Post-Ras Laffan damage, Qatar's ability to load and export LNG is materially impaired.

LNG-derived fertilizer feedstock price spikes compound the direct fertilizer import disruption. India's gas-based urea plants — which depend on imported LNG at Mundra, Hazira, Ennore, and Dahej — face input cost shocks hitting from both sides simultaneously.

cards.key_message: Fertilizer subsidies will balloon — the fiscal math breaks if crude stays at $146 AND fertilizer costs surge simultaneously

sub_messages.text: India's fertilizer subsidy bill was Rs 1.9 lakh crore in FY25. Higher import costs for urea and DAP, combined with government's mandate to hold retail fertilizer prices stable, will push FY27 fertilizer subsidies significantly higher.

FY27 fiscal deficit target: 4.3% of GDP. At $100 sustained crude, government expenditure rises ~Rs 3.6 lakh crore. Adding fertilizer subsidy expansion and LPG subsidy restoration means holding fiscal target requires deep infrastructure capex cuts.

The triple compression: fuel subsidies + fertilizer subsidies + LPG subsidies all expanding simultaneously while oil revenues from upstream PSUs collapse. Every energy sector C-suite should model their government dividend expectation at 50% haircut.

sub_messages.text: Quick Resolution (Scenario 1) probability: 5–10%. Both sides have publicly rejected ceasefire. Trump: 'Terms aren't good enough yet.' Iran FM: 'We never asked for a ceasefire.' This scenario is what ministries publicly pursue and privately consider least likely.

Prolonged Standoff (Scenario 2) base case: 35–40% probability. Hormuz closed through Q2, partial reopening Q3. Brent $100–130 range. Goldman Sachs Q4 Brent: $93/bbl under 2-month extended disruption. This scenario destroys OMC margins but allows survival.

description: Chronological: what happened → where we are → what's coming → what to do. Linear narrative.

cards.key_message: Operation Epic Fury erased the Strait of Hormuz in 12 hours — and rewrote the global energy order.

sub_messages.text: ~900 precision strikes on Feb 28 killed Khamenei, decapitated IRGC leadership, and triggered Iran's blanket closure of Hormuz by Day 1.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Animated horizontal timeline: 20:38 UTC Feb 28 (strikes begin) → Day 1 morning (Khamenei death confirmed) → Day 2 (Iran closure declared) → Day 4 (China-exemption announced) → Day 10 (Iran begins mine-laying confirmed by CNN). Each node annotated with actor + action.

sub_messages.text: Tanker traffic collapsed 70% within 24 hours. Maersk, CMA CGM, Hapag-Lloyd suspended all transits. 150+ ships anchored outside the strait.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Gauge dial: full arc = 20M bbl/d normal flow. Needle crashes to ~6M bbl/d by Day 5. Red zone shading below 8M bbl/d labeled 'Crisis Threshold.' Day counter embedded.

sub_messages.text: This is the largest oil supply disruption in history — 8M+ bbl/d offline by Day 10 vs. 5.6M in 1979 and 4.4M in 1973. No historical precedent for the scale or speed.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Horizontal bars for each historical crisis sorted by volume offline: 1973 Arab Embargo 4.4M, 1979 Revolution 5.6M, 1990 Gulf War 4.3M, 2019 Abqaiq 5.7M (brief), 2026 Hormuz 8M+. 2026 bar colored deep red, others gray. Duration annotated on each bar.

cards.source: Fars News, S&P Global, CNN, historical IEA records

cards.key_message: 42% of India's crude and 90% of its LPG imports just lost their primary highway — and there is no ready detour at scale.

sub_messages.text: India imports 5M bbl/d with 88.6% import dependence. Over 60% of crude and 90% of LPG flow through Hormuz. The strait is not a shipping lane — it is India's energy lifeline.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Sankey flow diagram. Left nodes: supply origins (Iraq 22%, Saudi 15%, UAE 6%, Qatar LPG, Russia 30%, West Africa 9%, Americas 6%). Right nodes: Indian ports (Jamnagar, Mundra, Kochi, Paradip, Vizag). Flow lines colored by Hormuz-transit (red) vs non-Hormuz (green). Red flows visually severed mid-stream with a barrier symbol at the strait.

sub_messages.text: LPG is the acute vulnerability: 330 million households depend on it for cooking. 90% of LPG imports transit Hormuz — a chokepoint with no viable bypass at any meaningful volume.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Fuel-tank style gauge: labeled 'LPG Import Security.' Full tank = 100% supply. Hormuz closure drains to 10% of import capacity shown as red liquid falling. Annotation: '330M households at risk.' Separate small tank labeled 'Crude' drains to 42% (non-Hormuz share blocked).

sub_messages.text: The $137B annual import bill — already India's single largest expenditure item — faces a structural shock before a single alternative ship has rerouted.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Waterfall: Start bar 'FY25 import bill $137B.' Positive steps: '+Hormuz disruption volume impact,' '+INR depreciation effect,' '+Freight premium.' Final bar 'Run-rate at $146 basket: $266B+.' Steps colored red. Net increment labeled '$129B incremental annual cost.'

cards.source: PPAC FY25-26, OPEC 2026 estimates, Ministry of Petroleum

cards.key_message: China's Hormuz exemption is not a diplomatic footnote — it is a 90-day competitive head start over every Indian refiner.

sub_messages.text: Iran declared Chinese vessels exempt on Day 4. By Day 15, China had moved 11 vessels through. India: 3. Japan and South Korea: zero. The geopolitical scorecard is now a procurement scorecard.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Regional map centered on Strait of Hormuz. Green ship icons with flag overlays: China 11 (clustered through strait), India 3 (at strait exit with escort icons), Japan 0 (ships shown anchored at Fujairah), South Korea 0 (anchored). Red barrier line across 21-mile strait. Numbered callouts: 1=China passage corridor, 2=India escort zone, 3=150+ ships anchor field, 4=Iranian minelaying zone (Mar 10).

sub_messages.text: India's 'non-alignment' delivers a marginal transit advantage over Japan and South Korea — but falls dramatically short of China's blanket passage. The gap compounds daily at 20M bbl/d of Hormuz flow.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Grouped horizontal bars per country: China (pre-crisis: normal access, now: 11 vessels, full exemption — green), India (pre-crisis: normal, now: 3 vessels case-by-case — amber), Japan (pre-crisis: normal, now: 0 — red), South Korea (pre-crisis: normal, now: 0 — red). Bars sized by effective access percentage.

sub_messages.visual_detail: Countdown tank: 'National Reserve Cover.' Total 74 days shown as liquid level. SPR portion (9.5 days) marked in dark blue at bottom. Commercial stocks (64.5 days) in lighter blue above. Red 'refusal line' at the top with label: 'India declined IEA/G7 release — every barrel being hoarded.' Day counter ticking from Day 1.

cards.source: Kpler, S&P Global, Iran state media, IEA press release March 2026

cards.key_message: Russia's 'discount' — the safety net that kept Indian refiners solvent through 2022-25 — flipped to a premium in 72 hours.

sub_messages.text: The OFAC waiver (March 5-6) unlocked ~30M barrels of Russian crude. Indian refiners moved fast: Reliance 10M bbl, IOC 10M bbl, BPCL/HPCL/MRPL buying the rest. But the price had already moved.

sub_messages.text: Urals shifted from $13/bbl discount to $4-5/bbl premium — a $17-18/bbl swing in landed cost. The emergency lifeline now costs more than the pre-crisis Saudi benchmark.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Side-by-side bars: 'February 2026' bar shows Urals at Brent -$13 (green, below zero line). 'March 2026' bar shows Urals at Brent +$5 (red, above zero line). Brent reference line drawn at zero. Delivered India west coast price annotated: $98.93/bbl (Argus March 14). Net swing arrow: '$17-18/bbl cost increase.'

cards.key_message: The mines are the longer war — they don't negotiate, and clearing them takes months after the last shot is fired.

sub_messages.text: Iran began laying naval mines on March 10. The EM-52 (Chinese-designed, rocket-propelled, 300kg warhead, acoustic sensors) defeats conventional minesweeping. The strait is operationally closed even before a single confirmed casualty.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Close-up map of the 21-mile strait. Shipping lanes marked. Mine field zones shaded red (confirmed) and amber (suspected). Numbered markers: 1=EM-52 deployment zone (deepwater channel), 2=US-sunk 16 Iranian minelayers (Day 11), 3=SADAF-01 moored mine zone (shallows), 4=21 confirmed Iranian ship attacks. Key callout: 'EM-52: non-magnetic composite hull — defeats standard US/UK minesweeping gear.'

sub_messages.text: Historical benchmark: Desert Storm 1991 took 51 days to clear 907 mines off Kuwait — AFTER the war ended, WITH the enemy's minefield maps, WITH full US/UK minesweeper deployment. None of those conditions exist today.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Comparison bars: '1991 Kuwait mine clearance' bar = 51 days (with maps, full assets, post-war peace). '2026 Hormuz clearance estimate' bar = 51-120+ days (no maps, assets degraded, war ongoing). Negative factors listed below 2026 bar: 'UK pulled last Gulf minesweeper home before crisis,' 'Best European assets months away,' 'EM-52 requires specialized non-magnetic gear.' Color: 1991 amber, 2026 deep red.

sub_messages.text: The UK Royal Navy pulled its last Gulf minesweeper home days before Iran laid mines. Columbia University: best European assets are 'months away.' The physical reopening window is at minimum weeks-to-months post-ceasefire.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Post-hostilities reopening timeline projection. Phase 1: 'Hasty single-lane clearance' (days to weeks, high risk). Phase 2: 'Minimum safe transit confidence' (weeks to months). Phase 3: 'Full commercial clearance' (months, possibly never complete — WWII mines still surface). Each phase bar colored from red to amber to green. Note at bottom: 'WWII mines still surface in North Sea — full clearance may never complete.'

cards.key_message: No negotiations. No back-channel producing results. Both sides have stated positions that are structurally incompatible.

sub_messages.text: Trump: 'Iran wants to make a deal and I don't want to make it because the terms aren't good enough yet.' Iran FM: 'We never asked for a ceasefire, and we have never asked even for negotiation.' This is not a negotiating posture — it is a statement of current reality.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Split-screen quote card. Left side (US flag): Trump quote in bold — 'Iran wants to make a deal, and I don't want to make it because the terms aren't good enough yet.' (March 15). Right side (Iran flag): FM Araghchi — 'We never asked for a ceasefire, and we have never asked even for negotiation.' (March 15, CBS). Bottom center: 'Zero active negotiations as of March 19, 2026.' Color: left = dark blue, right = dark green, center gap = red.

sub_messages.text: Iran's 3 formal ceasefire conditions (March 12): recognition of nuclear rights, war reparations for 1,200+ killed, binding international guarantees against future aggression. These are non-starters in Washington.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Decision tree rooted at 'Can conditions be met?' Node 1: 'Recognize Iran nuclear rights?' → US response: NO (NPT, Israel veto). Node 2: 'Pay reparations for 1,200+ killed?' → US response: NO (legal, political). Node 3: 'Binding non-aggression guarantee?' → US response: NO (Senate ratification impossible). All three branches terminate at red 'DEAD END' leaf. Overall assessment: 'Ceasefire preconditions structurally incompatible with US position.'

sub_messages.text: Mediators have failed: Oman sidelined after being blindsided by the strikes. China's Special Envoy Zhai Jun deployed but producing no results. Goldman Sachs now calls Quick Resolution 'the scenario every ministry publicly pursues and privately considers least likely.'
sub_messages.visual_detail: Four scenario mini-cards arranged horizontally: Quick Resolution (5-10%, green, $75-85 Brent) — labeled 'Privately least likely.' Prolonged Standoff (35-40%, amber, $100-130) — labeled 'BASE CASE.' Conflagration — Energy War (30-35% ↑ arrow, red, $130-200) — labeled 'Rising probability post-South Pars.' Democratic Iran (10-15%, gray, $80-100 long-term). Mediator status icons below each card (Oman: X, China: spinner, Turkey: X, Russia: X).

cards.key_message: Government invoked ESMA — refiners no longer control their own product slate. Every C3/C4 stream belongs to OMCs.

sub_messages.text: March 5: Government invoked Essential Services Maintenance Act powers. All propane, butane, propylene, butene streams must flow exclusively to OMCs for cooking gas. Petrochemical diversion is illegal — not just discouraged.

Label: 'ESMA override — effective March 5, 2026.'

sub_messages.text: 330 million households face 25-45 day refill gaps. Cities from Delhi to Chennai report 3AM queues, fistfights, and restaurant menu cuts. The LPG crisis is now a social stability issue, not just an energy one.

cards.key_message: India's 70% non-Hormuz claim is real but misleading — it covers crude only, and ignores a $17-18/bbl cost jump, grade mismatch, and 1.3M bbl/d that is structurally irreplaceable.

sub_messages.text: 70% non-Hormuz routing applies to crude only. LPG: 90% Gulf-dependent. LNG: Qatar ships virtually everything through Hormuz. The diversification headline conceals complete vulnerability in gas and cooking fuel.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Three parallel Sankey flows labeled 'CRUDE,' 'LPG,' 'LNG.' Crude: 70% green (non-Hormuz — Russia, West Africa, Americas) + 30% red (Hormuz — Iraq, Saudi, UAE). LPG: 10% green (US/Norway/Canada/Algeria emergency) + 90% red (Gulf/Hormuz). LNG: 5% green (spot, other) + 95% red (Qatar/Hormuz). Visual emphasis: LPG and LNG flows are almost entirely red. Header: '70% non-Hormuz claim — crude only. The other commodities tell a different story.'

sub_messages.text: The grade mismatch is structural: Indian refineries at Jamnagar, Kochi, MRPL, Paradip are configured for medium-heavy sour Gulf crude. Russian Urals is lighter. West African and US shale is light-sweet. Switching means running below capacity and losing diesel/bitumen yields.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Scatter plot: X-axis = API gravity (light right, heavy left, 20-45 degrees). Y-axis = sulfur content % (sweet bottom, sour top, 0-3.5%). Bubble size = volume India imports. Plotted crude grades: Iraq Basra Heavy (API 24, S 3.5% — large red bubble labeled 'Indian refinery sweet spot'), Arab Medium (API 31, S 2.6% — large red), Urals (API 32, S 1.5% — amber), Bonny Light (API 37, S 0.1% — small green), WTI (API 40, S 0.2% — small green), Buzios Brazil (API 28, S 0.4% — medium green). Shaded 'Indian refinery design zone' (heavy-medium, sour) in red rectangle. Most alternatives fall outside the zone.

sub_messages.text: 1.3-1.5M bbl/d of medium-heavy sour crude cannot be substituted regardless of route diversification. This is the hard ceiling — the irreplaceable volume that determines refinery throughput and margin.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Fuel tank gauge labeled 'Replaceable vs Irreplaceable Supply.' Total India imports = 5M bbl/d (full tank). Segmented: Green zone 'Substitutable via rerouting' = 3.5-3.7M bbl/d. Red zone at bottom 'Structurally irreplaceable' = 1.3-1.5M bbl/d, labeled with three sub-categories: 'Medium-heavy sour crude (1.3M bbl/d)', 'LPG at scale (no alternative)', 'Qatar LNG (no alternative).' Red zone cannot be emptied regardless of procurement action.

cards.section: THE NOW: EXPOSURE, PRICES, STRANDED SHIPS
cards.key_message: Macro damage is accelerating: current account, fiscal deficit, growth, and inflation are all moving in the wrong direction simultaneously.

sub_messages.text: At $146/bbl sustained, India's annualized crude import bill hits $266B — adding $129B of incremental cost. Current account deficit expands from projected 0.8% to potentially 2.5%+ of GDP. Rupee faces further downside from ₹92.64.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Waterfall: 'FY26 GDP impact chain.' Start: 'GDP growth baseline 7.2%.' Negative steps: '-0.4% (crude cost drain from CAD expansion),' '-0.3% (fiscal squeeze — Rs 3.6 lakh crore extra government expenditure),' '-0.2% (INR depreciation import amplification),' '-0.1% (inflation demand destruction).' Final bar: 'GDP growth at $130+ sustained: ~6.2%.' Labeled: '-100 bps total impact at $130+, 2-3 quarters.' Each step colored progressively darker red.

sub_messages.text: Inflation runs hot: CPI +40-60 bps per $10/bbl crude. WPI +80-100 bps. At $146 basket (vs $70 baseline), the pass-through math implies CPI is ~350 bps above baseline — partially absorbed by government price controls, but pressuring food, transport, and fertilizer costs.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Dual-axis line chart. X-axis: crude price scenario ($70, $80, $100, $120, $146, $200). Left Y-axis: CPI impact (bps above baseline). Right Y-axis: WPI impact (bps above baseline). Two upward-sloping lines. CPI line (blue): +0 at $70 → +150 at $100 → +280 at $120 → +380 at $146. WPI line (orange): steeper slope, +200 at $100 → +450 at $146. Vertical dashed line at $146 'TODAY' and at $200 'Conflagration scenario.' Shaded 'government absorption zone' shows portion suppressed by price controls.

sub_messages.text: Fiscal arithmetic breaks: FY27 deficit target is 4.3% of GDP. Every $10/bbl above baseline adds Rs 1.4-1.6 lakh crore in subsidy and expenditure burden. At $146, holding 4.3% means gutting infrastructure capex — the exact capex India needs to build supply resilience.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Matrix: X-axis 'Crude price' ($80-$100 → $130-$200). Y-axis 'Government response options' (subsidy absorption → price pass-through). Four quadrants: Bottom-left: 'Managed (pre-crisis norm).' Top-left: 'Fiscal stress — absorb costs, cut capex' (where India is heading at $146). Top-right: 'Crisis — forced pump price hikes, inflation spike.' Bottom-right: 'Pass-through allowed — inflation but fiscal relief.' India's current position dot sits in top-left quadrant with arrow pushing toward top-right. Note: 'No politically safe exit exists above $130/bbl.'

cards.key_message: April 3 is the single most important date in Indian energy procurement this year — and it is 15 days away.

sub_messages.text: The OFAC waiver expires April 3. If not renewed, India loses sanctioned Russian tonnage access — the backbone of the 30M barrels purchased this month and 25-36% of ongoing import supply.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Circular countdown gauge: large dial labeled 'Days to Russia Waiver Expiry.' Needle at 15. Scale runs 30 (green) → 20 (amber) → 10 (red) → 0 (black: 'Supply cliff'). Inner ring shows three concentric scenarios at expiry: Outer ring 'Renewed' (green) — 'India maintains 25-36% supply.' Middle ring 'Delayed 2 weeks' (amber) — 'Procurement gap, spot scramble.' Inner ring 'Lapses' (red) — 'Supply cliff: 1.3M bbl/d lost.' Current needle position: 15 days, in red zone.

sub_messages.text: Treasury Secretary Bessent's signal is conditionally positive but explicit: renewal is tied to India 'ramping up US crude purchases.' This is not a diplomatic courtesy — it is a transaction. The quid pro quo is on the table.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Two-panel quote card. Left panel (Bessent/Treasury): 'We fully anticipate that New Delhi will ramp up purchases of US oil' and 'India [is] good actors and essential partners.' Right panel (Congressional pushback): 'Dangerous, self-defeating, and indefensible' (Democrats on the waiver). Below both: Decision arrow — 'India must commit to US crude ramp-up to secure renewal. No commitment = no renewal.' Bessent quote sourced and dated. Color: left green (opportunity), right red (risk).

sub_messages.text: April 26 adds a second deadline: the Chabahar port waiver. India's only direct Iran trade route and a key non-Hormuz corridor is also subject to US sanctions architecture. Two waivers, one fortnight.
sub_messages.visual_detail: 15-day action timeline from March 20 to April 5. Key deadlines marked with vertical flags: March 21 — 'Stress-test procurement modeling deadline.' March 28 — 'Last safe window to lock Russian spot cargoes before logistics lead time.' April 3 — large red flag: 'RUSSIA WAIVER EXPIRY.' April 5 — 'First impact of lapsed waiver on supply chain.' April 26 — amber flag extending beyond frame: 'Chabahar waiver expiry.' Action items per CEO role annotated below each date.

cards.key_message: OPEC+ and IEA releases are political gestures — they cannot fix a closed strait or replace 8M bbl/d of physical flow.

sub_messages.text: OPEC+ approved 206,000 bbl/d increase for April. The spare capacity sits in Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Kuwait — all of which load via Hormuz. An extra 206K barrels you cannot ship through the strait does precisely nothing.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Three bars: 'OPEC+ April increase approved' = 206K bbl/d (small green bar). 'Hormuz flow reduction' = ~14-16M bbl/d (massive red bar extending far right). Ratio annotation: 'OPEC+ increase covers 1.3% of Hormuz shortfall.' Second bar set below: 'Saudi/UAE/Kuwait spare capacity location' — 100% labeled 'Behind the closed strait.' Note: 'Cannot physically reach market.' Bars make the futility viscerally clear.

sub_messages.text: IEA's 400M barrel release — the largest in the agency's 50-year history — covers only ~20 days of lost Hormuz volume and takes 120 days to fully deliver. It may calm markets; it cannot fix the disruption.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Waterfall: 'IEA Release vs Actual Need.' Start: Lost Hormuz flow at 20M bbl/d × 120 delivery days = 2,400M barrels total need. IEA release: -400M barrels (green bar going up, labeled '16.7% covered'). US SPR release 172M (green). Japan 80M (green). Germany 19.7M (green). Others ~130M (green). Net uncovered: 2,000M barrels (massive red bar still remaining). Bottom label: 'Even perfect execution leaves 83% of disruption unaddressed.' Timeframe: 120-day delivery window.

sub_messages.text: The market sees through the gestures: futures curve is in steep backwardation — $99 prompt WTI vs $69 December 2026 vs $58 2027. Markets expect a temporary shock, not permanent disruption. This creates a hedging opportunity that closes when ceasefire news breaks.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Futures curve chart: X-axis = contract month (March 2026 prompt through December 2027). Y-axis = price per barrel. Line starts at $99 (WTI prompt), slopes steeply down to $69 (Dec 2026), continues to $58 (Dec 2027). Second line: Diesel crack spread curve — $1,060 EUR/t April prompt, dropping to $620-650 (2027-28). Shaded 'Hedging opportunity zone' between current prompt price and Dec 2026 level. Annotation: 'Lock deferred crude at $69-75 Dec 2026 — backwardation creates a structural hedge book opportunity.'

cards.source: OPEC+ communiqué, IEA press release, Goldman Sachs, CME futures data March 19

cards.key_message: The fertilizer deadline is invisible — but May-June kharif season means the LPG crisis has a twin arriving in 60 days.

sub_messages.text: 50% of global urea production is disrupted (Iran + Qatar + Saudi supply chains). India imports significant volumes of fertilizer inputs from the Middle East. Kharif planting begins May-June — the deadline is hard and non-negotiable.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Agricultural calendar timeline overlaid on crisis timeline. Crisis timeline (top): Day 20 (today) → April 3 (Russia waiver) → April 26 (Chabahar waiver) → May (kharif planting). Agricultural timeline (bottom): March-April = 'Fertilizer procurement window.' May = 'Planting begins — fertilizer must be at mandi.' June = 'Sowing deadline.' Red convergence zone in May labeled: 'Procurement failure now = crop failure in June.' Annotation: '50% of global urea disrupted.' MUFG noted: India 40% fertilizer import from ME.

sub_messages.text: The five-deadline stack: Russia waiver (April 3), Chabahar (April 26), OPEC+ meeting (April TBD), Kharif season (May-June), and Q4 FY26 earnings (May). All five land within 75 days. No single deadline can be managed in isolation.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Horizontal 'deadline map' (timeline as geographic lane). Five numbered flags on the lane: 1=April 3 (Russia waiver, red), 2=April 26 (Chabahar, amber), 3=April TBD (OPEC+, gray — 'meaningless if Hormuz closed'), 4=May-June (kharif/fertilizer, orange), 5=May (Q4 earnings — 'OMC devastation'). Each flag has 2-line consequence annotation. Visual crowding of deadlines in April-May emphasized. Today (March 19) marked at left edge.

sub_messages.text: MUFG uniquely flags India's 40% fertilizer import dependence on the Middle East — a number almost no energy analyst includes in their India exposure model. Food inflation is the second-order shock that arrives 90 days after the oil shock.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Second-order shock waterfall: 'From oil shock to food inflation.' Step 1: 'Hormuz closed → urea/DAP supply disrupted.' Step 2: 'ME fertilizer supply -50% globally.' Step 3: 'India 40% fertilizer ME dependency (MUFG).' Step 4: 'Kharif planting disrupted.' Step 5: 'Food output drops.' Step 6: 'Food inflation spike (3-6 month lag).' Each step as a cascading red bar. Final bar: 'Food inflation +150-250 bps (6-month lag).' Source annotation: 'MUFG — only bank flagging this explicitly.'

cards.key_message: There are five scenarios. Only one is favorable. Two are base-case or rising. Your procurement, hedging, and capex decisions must survive all five.

sub_messages.text: Quick Resolution (5-10%): Brent $75-85, Hormuz reopens in 60-90 days post mine clearance. Every ministry publicly pursues this scenario. Every intelligence assessment privately considers it least likely.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Five scenario cards arranged in probability order. Card 1 'Quick Resolution': 5-10% probability (thin green border), Brent $75-85, timeline 60-90 days post-mine clearance, labeled 'Publicly pursued / Privately least likely.' Card 2 'Prolonged Standoff' (BASE CASE): 35-40% (thick amber border), Brent $100-130, closed through Q2, partial Q3. Card 3 'Conflagration': 30-35% ↑ (thick red border, upward arrow), Brent $130-200, closed through 2026, Gulf facilities damaged. Card 4 'Regime Change': 10-15% (gray border), Brent $80-100 long-term, 6-12 months war + reconstruction. Card 5 'De-escalation': 10-15% (light green), Brent $85-100, 90-120 days to reopen. Post-South Pars note: 'Conflagration probability rising.'

sub_messages.text: The base case (Prolonged Standoff, 35-40%) means Brent $100-130 through Q3. But the Conflagration scenario (30-35%) is approaching base-case probability after South Pars. The distance between the two is a Gulf facility strike.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Decision tree from 'March 19 status.' Branch 1: 'Iran retaliates on SAMREF/Jubail' → Conflagration (30-35%, $130-200, full 2026 closure). Branch 2: 'Iran restrains retaliation to Hormuz mining' → Prolonged Standoff (35-40%, $100-130). Branch 3: 'Oman/China broker surprise exit' → De-escalation (10-15%, $85-100). Branch 4: 'Internal Iran political shift' → Regime Change (10-15%). Branch 5: 'Trump accepts early deal' → Quick Resolution (5-10%). Each branch color-coded. Width of branch proportional to probability. Conflagration and Standoff branches are visually dominant.

sub_messages.text: Goldman Sachs raised US recession probability to 25% (from 20%) post-South Pars. A US recession at $130+ oil is a demand destruction wildcard that complicates every hedging strategy — it can cause a violent unwind of the war premium.
sub_messages.visual_detail: Scenario fan chart: X-axis = time (March 2026 to December 2026). Y-axis = Brent price. Five fan lines from current $108: Fan line 1 (thin green, 5-10%): slopes down to $75-85 (Quick Resolution). Fan line 2 (thick amber): ranges $100-130 (Standoff — fills most of fan space). Fan line 3 (thick red): rises to $130-200+ (Conflagration). Fan line 4 (gray dashed): drops to $80-100 after 6-month volatility (Regime Change).
